_comment: The shipped norm set. A norm is the normative distribution a measured value is graded
against, keyed by (measure, context, cohort) — NEVER BY ATHLETE ID. ALL NORMS HERE ARE
POPULATION NORMS.
That rule used to read 'never by athlete', which the optional cohort retires: a cohort is
a SEGMENTED population — men 55-64 — not a person. The part that survives is the part that
mattered. A norm that differs per player is a different feature with different storage and
a different UI, and nothing here should ever gain one.
mu is the centre; sigmaLo/sigmaHi are the tolerances either side (sigmaHi defaults to
sigmaLo when omitted, so a symmetric norm is written once). Asymmetry is normal, not
exotic — ball position forward is tolerated far more than back.
monitorLo/monitorHi are ABSOLUTE bounds on the Watch band and exist ONLY to reproduce
migrated content exactly: the old amber margin was a fixed number of degrees either
side of green, which is not a multiple of the green half-width and so cannot be
derived from the grade policy. Anything authored in the corridor editor omits them and
inherits the policy. If you are hand-writing a new norm you almost certainly do not
want them.
'unit' MUST match the measure's unit — a mismatch is a load error naming both sides,
never a silent grade.
CONTEXT: the GENERAL case is 'any', not 'full_swing'. A full swing is a shot TYPE, with no
more claim to being the default than a pitch or a bunker shot has, so a corridor that
applies to every shot is authored at the root. Resolution walks UP the tree from the shot's
own context and every context descends from 'any', so a row here is reachable from all of
them; a narrower row (per club, per archetype) still wins because the nearest row wins.
This was NOT true before: the general corridors sat at 'full_swing', which is a sibling of
'partial' / 'bunker' / 'specialty' rather than an ancestor. A pitch or bunker shot therefore
resolved NO corridor at all -- every reading came back not measured and no corridor signal
could fire, for a whole class of shot. Shot type must inform a diagnosis, never gate it.
So 'full_swing' now carries no rows of its own, and that is correct. Author there only when
something is true of a full swing and NOT of a pitch.
The wrist-grid rows below were migrated from the compiled table that used to live in
src/Analysis/reference_bands.cpp. That table, both of its providers and the parity gate
that pinned this file to it are all gone (stage 9): THIS FILE is the only place those
corridors exist, and nothing pins them any more. Re-seat them here.
They are STARTING HEURISTICS (design §11) — every number is expected to move once it
is re-seated against a corpus. They carry no citation because there is nothing to
cite; 'source: heuristic' with no n says exactly that.
The archetype_bowed / archetype_cupped rows are the face-corridor shift that used to
be a compiled ±10° offset for one DOF (kArchetypeFaceOffsetDeg, kept in
pp_tuned_constants.h only as the frozen record of what they were migrated from).
Bowed styles tolerate more bow and cupped styles more cup, so grading a valid style
against the neutral corridor would red-flag it. They override the general row on the
lead-wrist face axis ONLY; every other DOF is archetype-invariant and inherits.
SHAPE IS ON THE MEASURE, NOT HERE. A measure that grades only one tail is declared once
in core.json ('shape': 'floor' | 'ceiling'), because one-sidedness is a property of the
QUANTITY and cannot differ between a driver row and an iron row for the same measure.
Rows here carry only numbers. What a shape changes for an author is what those numbers
MEAN: on a floor, sigmaHi must equal sigmaLo (it grades nothing, and a load error names
it if they differ) and only monitorLo is legal.
plausibleLo/plausibleHi answer a DIFFERENT QUESTION from the corridor. The corridor asks
whether the swing was good; these ask whether the reading is real. A reading outside them
is not graded at all — not Action, not Ideal — because a driver smash of 1.62 is not a
swing finding, it is a mis-tracked ball, and grading it in either direction would launder
a capture fault into a confident diagnosis. They are on the ROW rather than the measure,
deliberately the opposite of shape, because the physical cap is context-dependent: smash
is bounded by loft, so driver, iron and wedge cap differently while all three are the same
one-sided quantity. Either bound may appear alone.
TEN measures are one-sided. m_smashFactor was the first; nine more were converted in the
unwatched-tails pass, where the question arrived from the other end — each was a measure
whose second tail GRADED with no fault behind it, so the choice was between authoring a
condition that does not exist and saying the tail is not a fault at all:
m_leadHandWidth          floor    a wider arc at the top is bounded by arm length
m_handSpeedP6P7          floor    see below — the sign question dissolved on inspection
m_pelvisRotRateP6P7      floor    the fault is the STALL; turning harder is not one
m_thoraxRotFinish        floor    the fault is an abbreviated finish
m_trailKneeFlex          floor    the fault is the trail knee STRAIGHTENING
m_comOverLeadFootFinish  ceiling  the fault is being off the lead foot, not on it
m_leadArmToTorso         ceiling  the fault is the arm leaving the torso — chicken wing
m_leadHeelLiftTop        ceiling  a planted lead heel is not a fault (its sigmaHi went
with the conversion: one tolerance on a one-sided row)
m_leadKneeFlex           ceiling  the fault is the knee buckling through impact
m_handSpeedP6P7 settles the sign question that was recorded here as open. The worry was
'deceleration or release-drag', which is a real ambiguity about hand SPEED — but the
measure is a RATE (mph/s, reducer rate over P6->P7), and its highMeans reads 'the hands
still accelerating into the ball'. More acceleration into the ball is not a fault at any
level, whichever side of the release argument you take, so the shape does not depend on
settling it.
One candidate was considered again and NOT converted, and the reason is the same one it
was refused for the first time:
m_xFactorStretch   stays target. The high tail is not free — it carries lumbar-load risk
— so calling it a floor would tell a golfer to keep going. The high
tail now carries a CONDITION instead, with the load in its injury note,
which is where a risk that is not a performance fault belongs.
m_lagAngleDown     genuinely TWO-SIDED: too little is casting, too much is a flip. Both
tails are faults, which is exactly what 'target' means — and the high
tail now has the condition to prove it.
Plausibility was NOT used to express any of this. A cap says a reading is not believed; it
never says a real reading is undesirable. Reaching for it to bound a loading risk would
put a swing judgement into the field that exists to keep swing judgements out.
COHORT-RELATIVE BIGGER-IS-BETTER MEASURES GET NO NORM AT ALL, and 'floor' is not the way
in. Ball speed, clubhead speed and carry are the cases people reach for first, and a
population floor on any of them grades a golfer Action for their age: the corridor would
be describing a population they are not in. They are BENCHMARKS — a different feature,
against a comparison group — and until that exists the honest answer is to report the
number and grade nothing. 'floor' is for self-normalising ratios and mechanically
universal thresholds only.
COHORT — the optional third term of the key. Absent on every row below, which means the
corridor describes everyone. Written as { 'sex': 'male'|'female', 'age': '<band>' } with
either field, both, or neither.
The age vocabulary is CLOSED: junior (under 18), adult (18+), and adult_18_54 /
adult_55_64 / adult_65plus beneath it. It is a fixed enum in code, changed only by a
schema version bump, and it is NEVER extended by pack content. That is the whole point:
this model is community-maintained and studies band age every way imaginable, so a free
numeric range would put one paper's arithmetic into the key where nothing could reconcile
it across packs. A study whose range does not match a band is mapped BY THE AUTHOR to the
nearest one, with the study's actual range recorded verbatim in 'citation' — the key stays
comparable and the provenance stays honest. Never widen the vocabulary to fit a paper.
'adult' is authorable in its own right and not merely a parent, because most provenance is
no better than 'adult male'. Without it the common case would need three duplicate rows
that then drift.
RESOLUTION IS CONTEXT-MAJOR. At each node of the upward context walk the cohort keys are
probed most-specific-first — sex+band, sex+adult, band, adult, sex, unqualified — and only
when none is present does it move up the tree. Two consequences, both intended: an
unqualified 'driver' row beats a senior row at 'any' for a driver shot, because stance
width is club-mechanical and if senior-driver matters it gets authored; and a senior row at
'any' answers wherever no club row exists, which is the ROM family, exactly where cohorts
matter. Age sits ahead of sex at equal specificity because the age effect on those measures
is larger and monotone, while sex differences are partly absorbed by the body-normalised
units the setup measures already use.
COHORT SHIFTS THE CORRIDOR AND NEVER INVERTS VALENCE — the same rule context obeys. If a
measure reads better high for one population it reads better high for all of them; what
changes is where the corridor sits, never which way is good. A cohort row that flipped the
direction would not be a corridor for a different population, it would be a different
measure wearing the same id.
BAND-EDGE CLIFFS ARE ACCEPTED. A golfer's grade can shift on their 55th birthday. There is
no interpolation between bands and there will not be: interpolating implies a continuity
the banded literature does not support, and the coach mediates the edge case exactly as
they already do for shot type. The 55 boundary is the seniors threshold in UK club practice
— a golfer already knows which side of it they are on — and it sits deliberately ABOVE
where the trunk-rotation decline literature pivots, so a 55+ row describes a population
that has unambiguously started to decline rather than one straddling the onset.
WHERE COHORT CONTENT WILL COME FROM, so nobody pads cohorts for symmetry. The rows that
want it are the RANGE-OF-MOTION family — thorax rotation, x-factor, the wrist ranges —
because age decline and sex difference are what that literature actually supports, and
because 16 rows below already rest on male-only samples (the professional benchmark curves
in 10.1123/jab.27.3.242 seat every thorax and pelvis rotation corridor) with nothing in the
schema recording it. They arrive with that review, not before.
The SETUP measures are largely cohort-INVARIANT and should mostly stay unqualified: they
are already body-normalised (% shoulder width, % stance width), so the normalisation has
absorbed most of what a sex axis would otherwise carry. Smash factor is self-normalising
and stays universal for the same reason. A cohort row authored on one of these to look
even-handed is a row nobody can defend and one more thing to re-seat.
And the rule above still holds: cohort-relative bigger-is-better outcomes get no norm at
all. A cohort corridor does not rescue ball speed — it would just be the wrong kind of
answer, segmented.

norms.citation: Measured from address to the top, then top to impact. Published tour figures are measured from the TAKEAWAY instead, so this metric reads a little higher than the 3:1 benchmark and a band cut for that basis sits slightly low for this one -- by the (small, structurally bounded, so far UNMEASURED) Address->Takeaway gap. Provisional until re-centred on a corpus. NB the low-side Watch band is empty: 1.8 is exactly -2 sigma, so a rushed transition goes Good -> Action at 1.8. Deliberate for now; revisit with the literature review. The 3.0 centre is reported in 10.48550/arXiv.physics/0611291 (ratio centred at 3.0 across all three golfer groups, with markedly smaller variance in playing professionals). NOTE that source is an arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed, AND measures from the start of motion rather than from address. Source stays heuristic for both reasons.

Migrated from the swing scorer's own impact band (pp_tuned_constants.h kFlexExtMu = 15.0, kFlexExtSigma = 12.0), which grades the ABSOLUTE sample at impact and was locked against a commercial wrist-sensor reference in Corpus 2. The scorer penalises only BELOW mu (cupping), which is exactly what sig_scooping detects; the two-sided corridor here is the conservative reading of the same figure. NB the sibling delta reduction (m_leadWristFlexExt_p7, the wrist-grid cell) carries mu 8.0, while this metric's howToRead implies a delta near 22.5 — see C1 in the implementation plan. That disagreement is about the DELTA and does not touch this absolute row. The high tail is graded as of the unwatched-tails pass (bowed_lead_wrist). The migrated scorer band penalises only below mu, so the symmetric 12 was the conservative reading of a one-sided figure and would have flagged a bowed-style impact that the archetype rows exist to accommodate. Estimate, awaiting a corpus.

Cap is the across-club ceiling, so a shot whose club is unknown still rejects an impossible reading. Ball speed cannot exceed clubhead speed by more than the coefficient of restitution allows, and the governing limit on that is a rule of the game rather than a property of any one club.

The cap is physics, not a corridor: a driver's low loft puts almost all of the strike into ball speed, and above roughly 1.56 the reading implies energy transfer the restitution limit does not permit. A higher figure is a mis-tracked ball or a mis-measured clubhead, not an efficient strike.

Loft-dependent: more loft sends more of the strike into spin and launch and less into ball speed, so an iron caps below a driver. The cap is a physical ceiling on the reading, never a judgement on the swing.

The most lofted case and so the lowest ceiling — a wedge converts the least of the clubhead's speed into ball speed. Also the noisiest in practice, which is why the tolerance is the widest of the four while the cap is the tightest.

Club unknown, so a deliberate no-op fallback: this corridor spans driver (about 2600) to wedge (about 9000) and is far too wide to ever fire. The per-club rows below are the ones that should resolve. Kept rather than deleted so an unknown club degrades to silence instead of to a missing norm.
